summary: The note surveys cybersecurity risks in augmented and virtual reality as of late 2023, covering vulnerabilities, threat categories, proposed standards, user education, corporate initiatives and international collaboration. It collects statements from experts at symposiums, studies and summits between September and December 2023. The central message is that AR/VR can only reach their potential if security is addressed proactively through technical frameworks, education, regulation and cooperation.
one_line: Overview of 2023 expert warnings and proposals for securing AR and VR platforms through standards, user education, corporate design and global collaboration.
key_facts: On September 12, 2023, the International Cybersecurity League held a symposium with keynote speaker Dr. Evelyn O'Donnell on cybersecurity in AR and VR.
Dr. Evelyn O'Donnell said "Immersive technologies are the new playground for cybercriminals" and warned of new phishing, data theft and psychological manipulation.
AR and VR platforms are especially vulnerable because they process large amounts of real-time data, including biometric data, location tracking and behavioral patterns.

A study published October 3, 2023 by CyberTech Analytics, headed by senior researcher Michael Svensson, examined how AR/VR vulnerabilities can be exploited, such as intercepting real-time AR feeds to superimpose misleading information.

Melanie Curtis organized the conference "The Future of Secure Immersive Tech" on October 15, 2023 and described four threat categories: Content Interference, Data Interception, Identity Theft and Hardware Manipulation.

On November 4, 2023, the Alliance for Secure Virtual Spaces (ASVS) proposed industry-wide security standards, including end-to-end encryption for all data exchanges and mandatory security auditing for AR/VR applications.
ASVS chairperson Jonas Kline said regularly updating security protocols is as important as the initial implementation.

Jennifer Chang, founder of the VR User Safety Initiative (VRSI), spoke on November 21, 2023 about user education; VRSI launched a global campaign on strong passwords, recognizing phishing in virtual environments and reporting breaches.

On December 1, 2023, a leading AR device manufacturer announced a "Secure by Design" initiative; CEO Larry Becker said it includes mandatory cybersecurity training for developers and a built-in incident response system in all devices.
Industry leaders are pressing for legislation enforcing strict cybersecurity standards for immersive technologies.

A global summit on December 12, 2023 brought together security professionals, tech companies, policymakers and user communities; cybersecurity liaison Alexei Petrov said "Collaboration is our strongest tool in creating secure immersive environments."
Experts at the December summit suggested forming a global cybersecurity task force specialized in immersive tech defense strategies.
